name: Li Chunfeng group subcommentary
summary: A Tang scholarly team led by Li Chunfeng wrote explanatory notes on the Nine Chapters and Liu Hui's commentary, presented to the throne in 656.
description: The Tang group’s subcommentary on the Nine Chapters and Liu Hui’s commentary, as transmitted in later collected editions.
tier_reason: Retain2: a later canonical subcommentary is not automatically negligible because it is textual. The source distinguishes substantive textual layers; a blanket specialist demotion is not established. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

impact.note: Official Tang teaching notes read by East Asian mathematical students; they clarify an existing text and little later work rests on them, implying tier 3 rather than 2.

why: The Tang state commissioned commentaries on the mathematical classics for its official mathematics teaching.

market.note: This node is scoped to mathematical knowledge and scholarly interpretation.

date.basis: Chemla reports that the scholarly group presented the subcommentary to the throne in 656.

events.statement: The group supervised by Li Chunfeng presented its subcommentary to the Tang throne.
events.caveats: The record identifies submission to the throne, but does not show that a particular ruler or official read or endorsed it, or prove dissemination beyond the court. Portions of received commentary layers may be blurred.

evidence.supports: Records the Li-led commentary’s presentation to the throne in 656.
Identifies it as a subcommentary on both the base text and Liu Hui.
